transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve been arranging my days around avoiding high bridges when I have to drive. If I can find another route, I take it, even if it’s out of the way. And if I can’t avoid it, I get through it, but I’m gripping the wheel the whole time.
Do you feel this same fear in other situations besides driving over high bridges?

Not really in other places, no. It’s mostly those high bridges over the bay. I know they’re built fine and people drive them every day, but when I get close to one, my mind just goes to, like, the car could go right over the side.
Have you ever had one of these intense panic episodes when you were not on or approaching a high bridge?
No, I don’t think so. It’s really tied to being on or getting close to those high bridges. I haven’t noticed it happening out of nowhere or in other situations.
Are there other situations where getting away might be hard that you avoid because of fear, like tunnels or elevators?
No, not really tunnels or elevators. It’s the high bridges when I’m driving. I plan my day around avoiding them, and if I can’t, I get through it, but I’m white-knuckling it the whole way.
